keyframe_review.note: 124,282 km2 for 1738-1799: 303 Tamil Nadu cells and 155 in Andhra Pradesh. The page gives no area. The shape holds through the Maratha raid of 1740-41, the Carnatic Wars and the 1773-1776 occupation of Thanjavur without change; it still contains 3 cells of the Madras area that the Chingleput jaghire (1763) took and the Madras Presidency page counts as the Company's first district (ledger loss). Many events of this long span (Wallajah 'had to surrender much of his territory to the East India Company', undated) are not on any page opened.

137,876 km2: the 1738 shape plus 48 cells at 78.6-79.8 E, 10.0-11.3 N, the exact area of the Thanjavur Maratha kingdom. That land did not pass to the Nawab: under the Treaty of 1799 'the administration of the Thanjavur kingdom was transferred entirely to the British East India Company' (Serfoji II page) and 'the territories of the Thanjavur Maratha kingdom were constituted as a separate district in 1799' (Madras Presidency page). Corrected to the 1738 shape; it ends with the Carnatic Treaty of 26 July 1801, so 1802 is outside the state's life.

correction.text: the 1800 shape without the Thanjavur kingdom, which went to the Company in 1799; valid 1800-1801

ledger.note: 1710: the Carnatic becomes an independent state under Saadatullah Khan I at Arcot. Infobox: 'Mughal subah (1692-1710), independent state (1710-1801)'; Saadatullah Khan I (1710-1732) was 'the last Mughal governor who was appointed as Nawab of Carnatic'. The page gives no 1713 date; it says the state ruled 'under the legal purview of the Nizam of Hyderabad' (not modelled as vassalage: no date).
1710: the court moves from Gingee to Arcot (infobox 'Arcot 1710-1768').
1734: the Nawab's expedition goes south against Madurai. 'The Nawab of Arcot sent an expedition south to demand tribute and fealty' (1734). The page does not say ground was taken that year.
1736: Madurai falls. 'Chanda Sahib declared himself king and imprisoned Meenakshi in her palace, ending the Madurai Nayakas for good.'

1736: the Carnatic annexes Madurai. 'Dost Ali Khan conquered and annexed Madurai in 1736.' The extent (Tiruchirappalli, Madurai and Tirunelveli country) is Cliopatria's 1738 addition; the Madurai Nayak page puts the same conquest to Chanda Sahib, the Nawab's son-in-law.

region.text: the former Madurai Nayak country, annexed

ledger.note: 1740: the Marathas invade the Carnatic. 'In 1740, the Maratha forces descended on Arcot'; they 'attacked the Nawab, Dost Ali Khan, in the pass of Damalcherry', Dost Ali and his son Hasan Ali were killed, Arcot 'surrendered to them without much resistance', and Chanda Sahib was sent to Nagpur.
14 March 1741: Trichinopoly surrenders to Raghuji Bhonsle (Maratha Empire page). The Maratha garrison and its end are on no page opened, so the land is not drawn as Maratha.

1762: Thanjavur becomes the Nawab's tributary. 'A 1762 tripartite treaty, mediated by the British, imposed a fixed annual tribute payable to the Nawab of Arcot, placing Thanjavur in political subordination.'

region.text: Thanjavur, subordinate to the Nawab of Arcot

ledger.note: 1763: Chingleput passes to the Company. 'Chingleput, obtained in 1763, was the first district in the Madras Presidency.' The page does not name the grantor; the Nawab is my reading (the English Colonial Empire dossier records the same gain from the Carnatic).
1773: the Nawab occupies Thanjavur. 'In 1773, troops of the Nawab and the East India Company occupied Thanjavur, and Thuljaji was deposed.'
1776: Thuljaji is reinstated 'on condition of hosting a British subsidiary garrison'.

1799: Thanjavur passes to the Company. Under the Treaty of 1799 'the administration of the Thanjavur kingdom was transferred entirely to the British East India Company'. The page does not say the tribute to the Nawab ended then; the year is the page's, the end of the tribute my reading.

26 July 1801: the Nawab Azim-ud-Daula signs the Carnatic Treaty, 'ceding tax rights to the British'. Madras Presidency page: he 'signed the Carnatic Treaty bringing the Carnatic region under British rule'; 'In 1801, the districts of North Arcot, South Arcot, Nellore, Trichinopoly, Madura and Tinnevelly were created'. The Nawabs continued as a princely state to 1855.

region.text: the Carnatic, brought under British rule by the Carnatic Treaty

wars.name: Carnatic-Madurai war (conquest of the Madurai Nayak kingdom)
wars.outcome: The Nawab's expedition of 1734 and the rebellion of Chanda Sahib ended the Madurai Nayakas in 1736 (infobox 'Disestablished: 1736'); the Carnatic annexed Madurai.

wars.name: Maratha invasion of the Carnatic
wars.outcome: Dost Ali Khan was killed at Damalcherry in 1740 and Arcot surrendered; Trichinopoly surrendered on 14 March 1741.
wars.note: The Carnatic Wars page is silent on this invasion, on the Nizam's 1743 action and on Anwaruddin Khan's appointment (the table gives his reign as 1744-1749).

wars.name: Carnatic Wars
wars.outcome: The French took Madras on 21 September 1746 and returned it in 1748; Clive took Arcot in 1751 (siege of Arcot 23 September - 14 November 1751); the Treaty of Pondicherry (1754) recognised Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah as Nawab; Wandiwash 1760, Pondicherry 1761, Treaty of Paris 1763. The pages date no change in the Carnatic's borders; the Chingleput jaghire is dated 1763 on another page.
wars.note: Muhammad Ali Wallajah 'became the ruler in 1749, however he was not officially crowned until 1752' and was recognised by the Emperor of Delhi in 1765 (Carnatic Sultanate page).

wars.name: Occupation of Thanjavur by the Nawab and the Company
wars.outcome: Thanjavur was occupied in 1773 and Thuljaji deposed; he was reinstated in 1776 with a British subsidiary garrison.

certainty.note: The pages give a province 'from the Krishna River to the Kaveri River' but no boundary; the southern limit after 1736 is Cliopatria's. No treaty line is drawn, not even the Carnatic Treaty's district list.

notes:
Five pages opened for the state itself (Carnatic Sultanate, Carnatic Wars, Nawab of the Carnatic, Madurai Nayak dynasty, Madras Presidency; budget up to 5) plus three pages opened for the other two dossiers of this batch (Thanjavur Maratha kingdom, Serfoji II, Maratha Empire). 'Carnatic Sultanate' and 'Nawab of the Carnatic' are the same state in two Wikipedia articles with near-identical text.

Start 1710, not Cliopatria's 1713: the infobox gives 'Independent state (1710-1801)' and Saadatullah Khan I (1710-1732); the Mughal dossier records the loss in 1710. End 26 July 1801 (the Carnatic Treaty, infobox), not Cliopatria's 1802; the Nawabs went on as a princely state until 1855, which is not drawn.

Cliopatria errors: (1) the 1800-1802 shape adds the whole Thanjavur kingdom (48 cells, same cells as its 1799 shape), which went to the Company in 1799; (2) the southern annexation is drawn from 1738 but the pages say 1736; (3) the 1738 shape keeps three cells of Madras that the Company held (Chingleput jaghire 1763).

Not settled: the Nizam's overlordship ('under the legal purview of the Nizam of Hyderabad', undated); the Nizam's 1743 intervention and the Maratha garrison at Trichinopoly 1741-43 (all four Carnatic pages silent); Muhammad Ali Wallajah's cessions to the Company ('had to surrender much of his territory', undated) and the Northern Circars (silent); Hyder Ali's 1780 invasion of Arcot (silent); the 1792 Seringapatam settlement (silent); the full list of Nawabs with reign years (the pages' table is mostly empty, so no ruler strip); the page budget left the shapes of 1718-1727 as identical copies of 1713.

Counterparts: nayaks-of-madurai (touches 1713-1737), maratha-empire, thanjavur-maratha-kingdom, english-colonial-empire and british-empire are all other batches or this one.
